items.t: Nintendo (OTCMKTS:NTDOY) Shares Break Below 50 Day Moving Average on Disappointing Earnings
sum: - Nintendo shares fell below their 50-day moving average after trading as low as $12.86; they last traded at $13.10 versus a 50-day average of $13.17.
- Quarterly results missed analyst expectations: EPS was $0.10 versus $0.11 expected, and revenue was $2.83 billion versus $2.94 billion forecast.
- Business signals were mixed: first-half net profit rose 11% on stronger software sales, while Switch 2 sales reportedly declined 41% year over year in fiscal Q2.

Nintendo Co. (OTCMKTS:NTDOY - Get Free Report)'s share price passed below its 50-day moving average during trading on Friday following a dissappointing earnings announcement. The stock has a 50-day moving average of $13.17 and traded as low as $12.86. Nintendo shares last traded at $13.10, with a volume of 1,615,288 shares changing hands.

The company reported $0.10 EPS for the quarter, missing the consensus estimate of $0.11 by ($0.01). The company had revenue of $2.83 billion during the quarter, compared to analysts' expectations of $2.94 billion. Nintendo had a return on equity of 16.31% and a net margin of 21.00%.

- Positive Sentiment: First-half net profit rose 11% year over year to 220.92 billion yen, supported by stronger software sales and expectations around the new Mario movie. Article: Nintendo's First-Half Profit Rose on Stronger Software Sales, New Mario Movie

- Positive Sentiment: A new The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launched for Switch 2, offering a potential boost to software sales, though launch performance was not yet reported. Article: Nintendo stock surges following Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launch

Nintendo shares a detailed look at first and third party game sales
sum: Following Nintendo’s most recent financial report, Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa has shared a look at what the first and third party sales situation is on Nintendo’s hardware platforms.

The graph above shows trends in software unit sales for Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2. The lighter colored portion represents the combined sales of new first-party titles that sold at least one million units in the fiscal year they were released. The darker color represents all other first-party software sales, as well as sales of software released by software publishers.

The sales breakdown shows that new first-party hits can significantly boost sales in a given fiscal year. At the same time, ongoing sales of our previously released evergreen titles, together with sales of third-party titles, provide substantial support for overall software unit sales. According to Nintendo, growth in their hardware installed base and user engagement has also supported an increase in software unit sales.

Nintendo also offered a look at the trends in unit sales and revenue for first-party software over the past 20 years. Since the launch of Nintendo Switch, unit sales of first-party software have remained consistently strong, supported by a large active user base. Revenue has also grown, reflecting a shift toward a business structure that consistently generates substantial revenue.

Japan's Nikkei 225 Begins Rebound as U.S. Stock Gains and Oil Price Plunge Offer Support, but AI and Semiconductor Shares Weigh
sum: The Nikkei 225 began trading higher on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on November 5, opening at 62,384.73 yen, up 196.10 yen (0.32%) from the previous trading day. Buying led the market, carrying over the momentum from gains in all three major U.S. stock indexes the prior day.

Two factors pushed the market up. One was the firm performance of the U.S. stock market as it digested the results of the U.S. midterm elections. The other was a sharp drop in crude oil prices as views spread that tensions in the Middle East were easing. Lower energy costs support investor sentiment through both corporate earnings and household burdens.
Among blue-chip shares, Toyota Motor (7203.T) surged, while Sony Group (6758.T) and index-heavyweight Fast Retailing (9983.T) were quoted higher.

On the other hand, artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor-related shares saw notable declines. SoftBank Group (9984.T), Tokyo Electron (8035.T), and Advantest (6857.T) all fell sharply, as caution over the direction of AI regulation continued to simmer.

In the previous day's trading on November 4, these three semiconductor and AI-related stocks alone pushed the Nikkei 225 down by about 1,241 yen at one point. Selling tends to concentrate in stocks with large index weightings, and this structure continues to amplify swings across the broader market.

Among market participants, the near-term focus is whether buybacks will emerge in the sharply fallen semiconductor shares. On the previous day, some stocks such as Fast Retailing and Nintendo (7974.T) rose, so the market was not uniformly lower. Some see the fact that buying interest is not one-sided as a sign of the market's underlying resilience.

On the overseas front, reports on vote counting in the U.S. midterm elections were also coming in during Tokyo trading hours, and market participants are focused on how U.S. long-term interest rates and foreign exchange rates react. Domestically, earnings announcements from companies such as IHI (7013.T), Mitsubishi Corp (8058.T), and NTT (9432.T) are scheduled during trading hours, and stock price reactions to individual earnings results could divide winners and losers within sectors.

Subnautica 2 Team Shares Intriguing Glimpse Into What’s Coming In Early Access 2
sum: We’ve been quite eager to know more about what Subnautica 2 is bringing to the waters in its Early Access 2.0 update, and the team has now obliged.

A new video highlights many interesting additions to the game, along with more information about the Collector Leviathan, including improved physics and the ability to operate each tentacle independently. Just something to remember when you think you’re safe and have evaded its grasp.

The Tadpole also gets a serious upgrade thanks to the Frog Chassis, which gives it arms and legs that change how you traverse the world. For example, it can climb, dash and even boasts a “very strong jump” that should make exploring the new region much smoother than with the Prawn Suit.

Of course, that’s not the extent of what’s new, and it’s quite an impressive set of additions (including one of the new Biomods). The new update is sure to help the game push its already solid sales record even further, which is a good thing, as it means more of you get to enjoy an experience that has had us quite addicted to what it offers.
Subnautica 2 is currently available for Xbox Series X/S and PC. Check out our early access review here.

Nintendo Shares Ocarina Of Time Switch 2 Design Sketches
sum: The latest Ask the Developer interviews are positively packed with interesting tidbits about the making of Ocarina of Time on Switch 2. One such story is all about the game's reimagined visuals, which Nintendo was even kind enough to share some initial sketches of.

According to Art Director Aya Shida, the team was consciously fighting a battle between making the game more realistic with the improved power of the Switch 2, and retaining the spirit of the original — a somewhat dark world, filled with weird characters. She therefore relied on phrases like “a puppet-show feel” and “the analogue feel of practical effects films” during development to reflect the goal: "both create a convincing sense that the characters truly exist within their respective fantasy worlds".

When it came to these characters, the team wanted to preserve their "familiar presence" first and foremost, before adding "designs unique to this game" on top. Hence, we end up with a recognisable Child Link, but with far more costume bells and whistles attached.
Here's a handful of the design sketches themselves, so you can see how the characters were initially conceptualised:

The same can be said for the game's iconic maps. "We didn't want to change the feel of each location or the way the locations connected with one another," Director HokWai Ng says in the interview, "both of which are so characteristic of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time". The team therefore went back to one of the artists who had worked on illustrations for the N64 original, and asked them to draw a new map for the game.
Such an approach resulted in the style we see today, which, we must say, has grown on us over the last few months — it really is quite the looker, eh?

One thing that is already rubbing some people up the wrong way, mind you, is how the game seemingly opts for SMAA over DLSS for its upscaling and anti-aliasing tech. Footage of the game's preloaded intellectual property notice has been doing the rounds on social media, where AMD FSR 1.0 and SMAA are listed under third-party technologies over Nvidia's DLSS. The same approach was taken on Donkey Kong Bananza, we should point out.

Video Game Stocks to Follow Oct. 31: 5 Names [2026]
sum: MarketBeat published its “Best Video Game Stocks To Follow Today” list on October 31, 2026, and the five names on it are not the ones most readers expect. Turtle Beach (TBCH), Allied Gaming & Entertainment (AIFA), Motorsport Games (MSGM), Brag House (HODO) and Alliance Entertainment (AENT) top the screen. Nintendo, Take-Two and Electronic Arts are absent, because the list ranks by trading activity rather than size. This analysis explains what the screen measures, what it leaves out, and which catalysts matter for video game stocks over the next three weeks.

The timing matters. Take-Two reports fiscal second-quarter results on November 9, and Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled to launch on November 19. Nintendo reaffirmed its annual forecasts on October 14, which we covered in our look at Nintendo’s 150% profit jump and 34% Switch 2 hardware drop. Against that backdrop, a list built on dollar volume is a starting point for research and not a buy signal.
What MarketBeat’s October 31 Video Game Stocks List Actually Says

The MarketBeat article states its method plainly. The five companies had the “highest dollar trading volume of any Video Game stocks within the last several days,” according to MarketBeat’s stock screener. That is the entire selection rule. It does not weigh earnings quality, valuation, analyst targets or growth.

A syndicated copy of the same list ran on the Daily Political site on October 31 with identical names and descriptions. Neither version gave a current share price, market cap or price target for any of the five stocks. The only analyst detail in the MarketBeat text is that Turtle Beach carries a Hold rating among analysts.

Those gaps shape how to read the story. High dollar volume tells you where money changed hands. It says nothing about direction, and volume spikes often follow news, retail enthusiasm or index flows. A stock can top this screen on a good day or a terrible one.

MarketBeat also ran a similar list on October 28, which shows the screen refreshes every few days and the cast of names can rotate. Readers who treat a single day’s list as a ranking of the best companies are reading more into it than the method supports.

Can Gaming Pipeline and Activision Add Momentum to Microsoft Stock?
sum: However, guidance points to a gradual recovery. For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Microsoft expects Xbox content and services revenues to decline in the mid-single digits, with hardware revenues also falling year over year. More Personal Computing revenues are projected to be between $12.2 billion and $12.7 billion. Management still expects Xbox to return to growth in fiscal 2027 as it resets its content portfolio, platform and operations.

Activision is already supporting profitability. In fourth-quarter fiscal 2026, More Personal Computing gross margin percentage expanded on lower amortization from the Activision acquisition. Yet Xbox revenues fell 10% year over year, as content and services declined 10% against a strong first-party comparable and hardware dropped 13%. Segment operating expenses rose 8%, partly reflecting Xbox impairment charges.
For fiscal 2026, Xbox revenues declined $1.7 billion, or 7%. Content and services slipped 5%, partly offset by Game Pass growth, while hardware fell 29% on lower console volumes.

The October releases and Call of Duty's premium launch model could support the anticipated second-half rebound in gaming. However, near-term revenues decline, ongoing restructuring costs and Xbox's roughly 5.5% share of Microsoft's $90 billion in fourth-quarter revenues suggest gaming alone is unlikely to be a major catalyst for the stock.

Listed U.S. rivals show similarly uneven near-term gaming trends. Take-Two InteractiveTTWO reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 net bookings down 3% to $1.39 billion. Yet Take-Two reiterated fiscal 2027 net bookings guidance of $8-$8.2 billion on the Nov. 19 launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, making Take-Two more dependent on one blockbuster than Microsoft. Roblox RBLX grew second-quarter 2026 bookings 8% to $1.6 billion and daily active users 10% to 123 million. However, Roblox expects third-quarter bookings to decline 14-18%, and Roblox has withheld revised full-year guidance amid softer per-user monetization, underscoring how pipeline timing is shaping sentiment across the sector.

MSFT shares have gained 10.4% in the year-to-date (YTD) period compared with the Zacks Computer – Software industry’s 0.1% return. The Zacks Computer and Technology sector has appreciated 19.3% in the same time frame.

'It Takes Two' Hops Onto Switch 2 Next Week, Marrying Visual Upgrades & Cross-Play
sum: After being rumoured earlier this year, Hazelight has announced that its award-winning co-op adventure, It Takes Two, will be getting a full Switch 2 upgrade next week.

The new version launches on 15th October, as a free upgrade to anyone who owns the Switch 1 version. Naturally, the Friend's Pass will be sticking around too, so you'll be able to play with a pal even if only one of you owns it.

The game boasts enhanced graphics and performance on Switch 2 (1080p and 60fps in Docked Mode), faster load times, and even more ways to play together thanks to GameShare. Hazelight has also announced that it'll be launching cross-play support on the very same day, so you'll be able to play the Switch 2 version with friends on PC, Xbox Series, Xbox One, PS4 or PS5.

Such cross-play features won't be quite as expansive for anyone playing on Switch 1 — where you'll only be able to play online with a Switch 2 player if they downgrade to the OG Switch version — but hey, the launch is all about the new hardware, at the end of the day.

"Now-standard graphical compromises have been made for Switch, and the typical perk of playing handheld is questionable for an always-split-screen co-op-only game," we said of the Switch 1 version back in 2022. "Nonetheless, it keeps the frames moving well enough not to undermine its Game-of-the-Year sparkle."
With some visual polish on Switch 2, we might even be tempted for another playthrough.

Update | GTA 6: Huge New York mural nearly complete, artist shares details
sum: The location is particularly interesting. Rockstar reportedly used the same corner for a GTA 5 mural back in 2013, and earlier Grand Theft Auto games were also promoted with elaborate hand-painted building façades. Rather than simply being a convenient advertising spot, the Brooklyn location may therefore be a deliberate nod to a long-running Rockstar tradition. A short video has since surfaced on Reddit showing the mural taking shape. While much of the artwork is still unfinished, parts of the background have already been painted in color:

The similarities to the GTA 5 campaign do not end with the location. That mural also appeared only a few weeks before the game launched and was accompanied by a broader wave of outdoor advertising across New York. Rockstar returning to the same corner 13 years later, once again just weeks before a GTA release, is therefore fueling speculation that the company is entering the final stretch of its marketing campaign.

That is certainly how many fans on Reddit are interpreting it. With GTA 6 (available for pre-order on Amazon) only weeks away and Rockstar seemingly following a familiar playbook, hopes are growing that October could bring more promotional material – whether additional screenshots, gameplay footage or even a new trailer. For now, however, Rockstar has not announced anything of the sort.
Artist reveals when the GTA 6 mural is expected to be finished

There are now not only new images showing the mural's progress, but also some interesting firsthand information. Artist u/Omfish has spoken out on Reddit, claiming to be personally involved in the project. According to him, the mural is expected to be completed as early as Friday, October 9, provided the work progresses as planned.

The large-scale mural reportedly requires a total of one to two weeks of work, with daily shifts lasting eight to ten hours. The artist also explains that he is working on the project as a freelance muralist for a company called Colossal, which, according to him, was previously involved in creating hand-painted advertisements for GTA: San Andreas. Another surprising detail concerns the mural's lifespan. According to Omfish, it is a temporary advertising installation that is expected to remain in place for only about a month.

Nikkei 225 Today, September 16: Index Rises Above 64,200 After Fed Decision As Yen Weakness Boosts Exporters; Check Why Japan Stocks Are Rising And Top Components
sum: Japanese shares moved higher on Thursday, with the Nikkei 225 gaining 0.52% and trading above the 64,200 mark. The broader Topix index also advanced around 1% to reach 4,100. The gains came despite the latest US Federal Reserve decision, while a weaker yen helped improve the outlook for Japanese companies that generate significant revenue from overseas markets.

The decline in the yen against the US dollar supported export-oriented companies by improving the value of their overseas earnings when converted into the Japanese currency. Japanese equities also received support from softer oil prices. Lower crude prices could ease costs for an economy that relies heavily on energy imports.
The JP225 was trading at 64,258, up 335 points or 0.52% during the session. The index has gained 41.89% over the year, although it remains down 4.71% over the month based on the latest market data.
Several major companies listed on the Nikkei recorded gains during Thursday’s session.
Among the major stocks, Tokyo Electron and Advantest were trading lower, falling 1.78% and 1.56%, respectively.
Mitsubishi Heavy Industries rose 3.1%, while Nintendo gained 3.3% in the latest session. Fujikura also advanced 2.7%. SoftBank Group gained 1.2%, while Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group added 0.6%.

The Nikkei 225 is a price-weighted stock market index that tracks 225 major companies listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. It was established with a base value of 176.21 on May 16, 1949. The index is widely used as a key indicator of Japanese equity-market performance. The quoted JP225 figure can differ from official exchange data because derivative-based market references, including CFDs and futures, may be used by some financial platforms.

Nintendo stock price tumbles after Direct despite demand for Zelda Switch 2 console
sum: Fans expressed enthusiasm after learning Nintendo Direct showcases would air on consecutive days. However, investors haven’t reacted as positively to the September 8th and 9th broadcasts. The Nintendo stock price in Japan fell 3.99% following the Zelda 40th Anniversary showcase. It then dropped another 4.90% 24 hours later, despite welcoming a healthy lineup of Switch 2 games.

U.S. trading under the NTDOY ticker was also down 1.21% on September 8th and another 5.76% a day later. The first Nintendo Direct honored a celebrated series and confirmed the Ocarina of Time remake release date. Pre-orders opened for the title, as well as the Zelda Switch 2 console and Pro Controller. Both sold out at retailers, benefiting scalpers.

The less predictable September 9th show highlighted a bevy of third-party projects. Viewers saw trailers promoting major IPs like Final Fantasy, Monster Hunter, and Resident Evil. Still, shareholders already knew about many of these releases before the event.

Traders monitoring the Nintendo stock price often focus more on first-party Switch 2 game announcements. Exclusive software can lure players away from the competing Xbox and PlayStation ecosystems. Leading up to the Nintendo Direct, leaks about 3D Mario and Super Smash Bros. entries surfaced.

The Japanese gaming giant unveiled free Mario Kart World DLC and updates or upgrades for Star Fox, Pokémon Pokopia, and Pikmin 4. Yet new game reveals were limited to Metroid Ravenous and Kirby and the World Beyond.

The Metroid Dread sequel has been well received, and its Special Edition with Samus amiibo has proven popular at storefronts. On the other hand, while Kirby is an established franchise, investors may not view it as a console seller. Many fans have also grown frustrated by the lack of a Super Mario Odyssey sequel.

A more expensive handheld has raised questions about profits heading into 2027. The Switch 2 rose from $449.99 to $499.99 on September 1st in the U.S. following a price increase that hit Japan in May. Speculators considering Nintendo stock have to decide whether the newly announced titles will attract enough adopters.

Nintendo shares the first teaser for live-action Legend of Zelda movie
sum: During their 40th Anniversary Direct, celebrating four decades of the Zelda franchise, Nintendo finally addressed the long-gestating live-action Legend of Zelda movie. The reveal, though, landed somewhere between anticlimactic and mildly informative for fans who'd spent the past week bracing for a first trailer.

The film's official title is “The Legend of Zelda”. No subtitle, despite the games routinely carrying one (Ocarina of Time, Breath of the Wild, and so on). Shigeru Miyamoto explained the choice, saying the movie tells an original story that pulls from ideas across the franchise's 40-year history rather than adapting one specific game, and that fans would understand the choice.

Outlets across the gaming press speculated in the run-up to the Direct that a full trailer would premiere during the broadcast. That didn't happen. The Direct's real centerpiece was the Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2, which got a full gameplay walkthrough and a November 5 release date. Multiple outlets covering the livestream noted the segment was limited to the new title card and a reconfirmation of the April 30, 2027 release date, along with a note that future updates will run through the Nintendo Today app first.

Fans on Reddit were not thrilled with the lack of a proper trailer, with some commenting on a post sharing the news: “I was sure they would have something for the movie by now.” For now, fans will have to adjust their expectations for a proper trailer closer to release and hope the movie can live up to the game’s legacy.

sum: Find your next quality investment with Simply Wall St's easy and powerful screener, trusted by over 7 million individual investors worldwide.

Nintendo stock has delivered a 74.8% gain over the past five years, yet current valuation checks suggest there may still be a discount left in the price, as both the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) intrinsic value estimate and market multiples point to shares trading below their assessed worth. - On Simply Wall St's checks, Nintendo screens as undervalued in 3 of 6 tests. This gives a mixed picture on whether the stock is a clear bargain or closer to fairly priced overall. See the 3 out of 6 valuation score for detail.
The issue now is whether the current share price already reflects the recent profit strength or if the intrinsic value estimates still point to a margin of safety for Nintendo.

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model estimates what Nintendo is worth based on the cash it can generate for shareholders over time. Kyoto-based Nintendo Co. reported Thursday 147.4 billion yen ($933 million) in April-June profit, up from 96 billion yen in the same period a year ago.
Quarterly sales dipped 9.5% to 517.8 billion yen ($3.3 billion).
Working as a negative for Nintendo, as with many Japanese companies, were U.S. President Donald Trump’s tariffs, as well as the rising price of memory chips and other components.

Nintendo is forecasting 310 billion yen ($2 billion) in profit for the full fiscal year through March 2027, down nearly 27% from the previous fiscal year, on annual sales slipping 11% to 2.05 trillion yen ($13 billion).

In Switch 2 software, “Yoshi and the Mysterious Book,” released in May, and “Pokemon Pokopia,” released last year, were popular, leading to software sales totaling 9.46 million units for the quarter, according to Nintendo.

sum: On July 29, Nintendo (7974.T) shares rose for a third straight session on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, closing at ¥8,058, up ¥399 or 5.20% from the previous day. The last time the stock closed above the ¥8,000 level was April 28, roughly three months ago. As semiconductor memory giant Kioxia Holdings (285A.T) plunged sharply, investment funds clearly rotated back into game stocks that had been sold off on the view that soaring memory prices would weigh on earnings.

Led by Nintendo's advance, game-related stocks rose across the board. Buying spread to Konami Group (9766.T) and Square Enix Holdings (9684.T), with notable fund inflows into the entire sector. Market participants noted that "funds that had been concentrated in semiconductor memory-related names are now shifting to game stocks, which had been relative laggards," according to a domestic securities analyst. Game industry media outlet gamebiz reported that Konami Group and Square Enix Holdings ranked among the top gainers in the morning session on July 29, confirming the broad-based inflows into the gaming sector.

Meanwhile, Kioxia Holdings shares were at one point sold down to the ¥37,000 range on July 29, representing an intraday decline of more than 10%. The drop from its all-time high of ¥112,700 reached on June 22 now exceeds 60%, completely erasing the gains accumulated after its previous earnings announcement. Changes in the business environment surrounding semiconductor memory are fueling investors' bearish stance.

That said, Kioxia shares did experience a brief surge immediately after the market opened on the same day, touching ¥48,820, up ¥4,270 or 9.58%, in what turned out to be an extremely volatile session. Nintendo Tariff Lawsuit: Sony Sued, Stock Falls 4% [2026]
sum: Nintendo told a federal judge this week that its customers have no legal claim to a share of the tariff refunds it may soon collect from the US government – a defense filed one day before Nintendo’s Tokyo-listed shares dropped 4%. The July 21, 2026 motion to dismiss is Nintendo’s answer to Hoffert et al. v. Nintendo, a proposed class action accusing the company of “double-dipping”: raising Switch and Switch 2 accessory prices in 2025 to cover tariffs a court later ruled illegal, then separately suing the federal government to get those same tariff payments back.

Sony faces a nearly identical accusation. Walker et al. v. Sony Interactive Entertainment, filed in the Northern District of California, claims Sony pocketed a “substantial windfall” by raising PlayStation 5 prices by as much as $200 per unit with no plan to pass along whatever refund the government eventually pays. Together, the two suits turn a routine 2025 pricing story into one of gaming’s biggest unresolved legal fights of 2026: who actually owns the money from an illegal tariff, once the price increase it justified is already sitting on a customer’s receipt.
The Accusation: Nintendo and Sony Accused of ‘Double-Dipping’ on Tariffs

Both lawsuits rest on the same legal theory: unjust enrichment through “double recovery.” In 2025, the Trump administration imposed sweeping tariffs on imported goods under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), and both Nintendo and Sony responded by raising prices on tariff-exposed hardware, citing “changes in market conditions” and a “challenging economic environment,” respectively. Neither company named tariffs directly in its pricing announcements, but plaintiffs in both the Nintendo tariff lawsuit and the Sony case argue the timing makes the connection obvious.

The twist arrived in February 2026, when the US Supreme Court ruled the Trump administration had exceeded its authority in imposing the IEEPA tariffs, invalidating them. The federal government subsequently stood up a $166 billion refund program covering roughly 300,000 importers across every sector of the economy, not just gaming. Nintendo moved quickly to claim its share, suing the government in March 2026 for its own refund, with interest.

sum: - Google's Vice President of Devices and Services, Shakil Barkat, blamed pressure from soaring memory chip prices.
- Alphabet published an upbeat earnings report last week, but its stock fell because of the company's decision to raise its capital expenditure target.

A top Alphabet, Inc. executive has indicated that Google will raise prices of its Pixel phones thanks to soaring memory chip prices that have triggered price hikes across products from Apple to Nintendo.
In an interview with 9to5Google, Google Vice President of Devices and Services Shakil Barkat all but confirmed that the company faces pressure to raise prices.

Barkat emphasized that, like all other consumer technology companies, Google is experiencing an unprecedented surge in costs, noting that "there's never been an increase in memory prices like the world's going through right now." He pointed to Morgan Stanley data about a sixfold increase wherein 1 GB of RAM went from $2.80 in 2025 to $12 this year.

Google has "shielded our consumers from supply fluctuations for as long as possible." However, the "economics have fundamentally shifted, and we're not immune to that," Barkat told the tech news site.

As such, the entire Pixel family of devices will see price "adjustments" that "will be rolled out dynamically to match supply realities." This includes the upcoming Pixel 11 series, though the company won't be sharing specifics until the Aug. 12 announcement. Google's hardware portfolio also includes the Pixel Watch.

Who Owns Nintendo?
sum: Nintendo is one of the most popular gaming companies in the world. The publisher and developer has created games including "The Legend of Zelda," "Super Mario Bros," and "Pokémon." However, before it made consoles, hardware, and video games, Nintendo began by making and selling playing cards in Kyoto, Japan. The company was originally founded in 1889 by Fusajiro Yamauchi and is a publicly traded entertainment and video game business owned by shareholders, but it's more complex than that.

The first console Nintendo released was the 1983 Family Computer (Famicom) system in Japan. Today, it manufactures the fastest-selling console in Nintendo's history, the Nintendo Switch 2, and a few other products that aren't the Switch. As for who owns Nintendo, well, it's largely owned by major shareholders and minor shareholders. The major shareholders are listed on Nintendo's website and include the following: The Master Trust Bank of Japan, Ltd. (Trust Account), Custody Bank of Japan, Ltd. (Trust Account), JP Morgan Chase Bank 380752, The Bank of Kyoto, Ltd., State Street Bank and Trust Company 505001, and more. The shares are split between each individual company and owner.

Nintendo releases annual reports detailing its sales, shareholders, and other additional details regarding the company. As for the people who are in charge of the day-to-day procedures at Nintendo, the company has had several leaders who have made some major waves in the industry.

Today, Nintendo is run by President and Representative Director Shuntaro Furukawa. He's a Japanese businessman who is currently the company's sixth president, which is impressive as the company has been around for 137 years. He replaced Tatsumi Kimishima, after Kimishima's retirement in 2018, who took over after the death of Satoru Iwata. As President of Nintendo, Furukawa oversees the entirety of Nintendo, including Nintendo of America.

He oversaw a few of Nintendo's most recent games and served as executive producer on "Star Fox," "Pokémon Pokopia," and "Metroid Prime 4: Beyond." As the head honcho of Nintendo, Furukawa is also responsible for everything the company makes, even if it chooses to make something odd like it did with the Virtual Boy, which is one of the weirdest products ever made by Nintendo.

items.t: Square Enix shares new details about Final Fantasy Resonance, including characters, maps, and battle mechanics
sum: Along a new trailer today, Square Enix has uploaded a ton of new information regarding Final Fantasy Resonance, the upcoming HD-2D RPG. Posing the question, “What if Final Fantasy had continued to push the limits of pixel art?”, the trailer is mostly a look at the visual design of the game. I don’t think it actually works that well, as the backgrounds are far too clean to evoke old school charm, but that’s neither here nor there. The majority of information today comes from a massive press release, which practically gives away the entire introduction.

Weirdly omitted from the trailer, Square Enix details the worlds players will be traversing, which include Dilmagia and Olderion. Dilmagia, aka the Machinopolis, is reminiscent of Final Fantasy 6’s overall design, and serves as the birthplace of the airship. Longtime Final Fantasy stalwart Cid also used to call the city his home, though has since left to explore the rest of the world.

Olderion, meanwhile, is more of an aquatic city. Known as Aquapolis, it functions as the capital of the Olderion Federation, and is blessed with abundant waters. A coalition known as the Warders of the Waders have maintained peace in the city, helping to protect its citizens alongside the “Maiden of the Water” and an esper called the “God of Water.”

Next in the press release is a section about new characters players will encounter. They include Lid, an airship engineer from Dirnado who has been helping out her family from a young age. She, along with her brother, have become quite adept engineers, and are on track to rival even Cid in terms of skill. There is also Nichol, a strategist from the Olderion Federation with a passion for defending his homeland. Raised in a family of Wardens, Nichol is tactical and objective, though never loses his composure.

The final new characters Square Enix divulged information on are the majestically titled Veritas of the Heavens and Veritas of the Waters. The duo are both members of the Sworn Six of Palandia, which has given them a ruthless desire to destroy crystals. Heavens utilizes a mixture of lance techniques to dominate opponents, while Waters is more free-form with their combat.

items.t: Gonna buy Take-Two shares before the GTA 6 release? Here's how blockbuster game launches actually move stocks
sum: Grand Theft Auto VI pre-orders opened at midnight on June 25, and the most anticipated video game in history now has a firm launch date: November 19, 2026.

The immediate temptation for investors is obvious. This is the biggest upcoming entertainment launch of the decade — Grand Theft Auto as a franchise has sold north of 470 million copies. And Rockstar is already guiding to record revenue. Surely the move is to buy Take-Two Interactive (NASDAQ:TTWO) and ride the wave, right?
By signing up, you accept Moneywise Terms of Use, Subscription Agreement, and Privacy Policy.
Even Take-Two's CEO is uneasy. Strauss Zelnick has called the launch "terrifying" because the expectations are so high.

Take-Two stock rallied in the week leading up to pre-orders. Then it fell nearly 3% the moment they actually opened. A standard edition priced at $79.99 came in below the $90-to-$100 some bulls had hoped for, and short-term traders did what they almost always do when there’s a confirmed catalyst: they took profits and left. Unconfirmed reports put first-day pre-orders as high as 39 million and $3 billion in revenue — numbers neither Take-Two nor Rockstar has confirmed. The stock fell anyway.
Stocks move on the gap between expectation and reality, not on raw sales. By the time you've heard a game is going to be huge, the "huge" is already in the price.
Here are four cases that show how this plays out — including one from Take-Two's own history.

items.t: Nintendo's president shares comments on Nintendo's current stock slump
sum: Not that long ago we saw Nintendo stock hit its highest point ever, and just a few weeks later it broke yet another record. Fast-forward to today and we’ve seen Nintendo’s stock drop considerably. It’s been a hot topic across all sorts of financial publications, and now Nintendo themselves are chiming in on the situation.

During a Nintendo shareholder Q&A Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa addressed the stock slide that Nintendo has been seeing for a few months now. According to Furukawa, Nintendo stock is now about half of what it was during its all-time high. In Furukawa’s opinion, the stock has fallen due to a number of external factors, and he believes the market is viewing the company critically due to moves such as raising the Switch 2 price.

Furukawa went on to say that Nintendo’s goal right now is to continue pushing Switch 2 and further popularize the platform. They’d like to build long-term relationships with customers, which will help Switch 2 reach even further, and then in turn, the platform’s success should help turn Nintendo stock around. Whether or not that actually happens remains to be seen.
